spec: reports/plans/2026-11-23_plan_p2-67-adl-spec.md (GPT plan review: ready to run option A; redteam-lead amendments of 2026-11-23 folded in below)
descriptive: user via whip-lead 2026-11-23: the faithful ADL is reported as what it reads on our fine-tunes; no reuse/new verdict comes from ADL under either wording of the definition

control.what: the authors' toolkit at 617d9266, unchanged, on the paper's Qwen3-1.7B panel (Fig. 7 / Fig. 32 as plot_causal_effect.py ~L1599-1625 builds it): 3 organisms x 2 variants, the spec's resolved command (experiments/adl_published/pod_control.py `command`)
control.a_rule: training data, default: the three-organism mean incr_ce is above the three-organism mean random_diff_mean at >= 5 of positions 0-8, AND its mean over positions exceeds the random mean's by > 2 sd of the 64 random differences (each random k's incr_ce averaged over organisms and positions; sd over k). Paper: 'clearly positive on D_ft', 'random diff vectors yield causal effects close to zero'
control.b_rule: FineWeb, default: the three-organism mean incr_ce is below 0 at >= 5 of positions 0-8. Paper: 'negative for Qwen3 1.7B'
control.c_rule: training data: mix1-2p0's position-mean of the three-organism mean incr_ce over default's is in [0.25, 0.75]; undefined (a miss) when default's is <= 0. Paper App. F.8: 'roughly half'
control.d: descriptive: mix1-2p0's FineWeb position-mean is expected slightly positive
control.on_miss: a miss on (a), (b) or (c): the pinned toolkit does not reproduce the paper's Qwen panel; stop, report, no 67M items
control.run_time_checks: pod_control.py checks: HEAD is 617d9266, mix1-2p0 is listed for qwen3_1_7B in all three organism configs, the Qwen3 tokenizer adds no BOS (bos_token null, tokenizer_config add_bos_token false); a miss exits 3 before any run
control.checker: experiments/adl_published/control_check.py -> results/control.json, with every organism's curve beside the mean

parity.what: the port (commute.adl_ce through parity.py's HFPair) against the toolkit on cake_bake default, inputs built by the toolkit's own functions (sha256 recorded; counts asserted equal to the toolkit's saved counts)
parity.bar: per kind of number (delta_bar entries; CE_ft, CE_base, CE_swap, incr_ce), port-vs-toolkit max |difference| <= the floor, the max |difference| between two fresh toolkit runs (run A = the control's cake_bake default, run B = the floor run). A floor of exactly 0 gives no bar: reported, no pass claimed
parity.floor_run: the same command with diffing.method.batch_size=16 diffing.method.causal_effect.batch_size=4 (the toolkit is deterministic run to run on one card, so an identical rerun gives a zero floor; batch shapes are the one change that moves bf16 rounding and nothing else)
parity.not_compared: the 64 random differences and 64 Gaussian vectors (the toolkit does not save them)

settings.like_positions_source: spec 4.2 like-for-like rule: the same five positions' masks (j = 0-4, E264-267's k = 5)
settings.doc_tok_source: toolkit n 128 (a document is kept with >= n tokens, cut at n * 10 characters, method.py L101-106)
settings.batch_source: E264-267's delta_bar batch (memory only; the mean is summed in float64)
settings.eval_batch_source: memory only (67M logits at 512 tokens x 50k vocab, fp32, with the log-softmax copy: ~7 GB per batch)
settings.random_diff_rows_source: the toolkit pools the valid positions of one batch of 16 texts once it holds >= 2n (causal_effect.py L436-441); here 16 Pile val rows of 512 tokens (E264's rows 8176-8191), as the 67M has no chat template for tulu (spec: 67M forces)
settings.n_train_source: ours: the first 256 training windows of each state, so ~180 states fit two 30-min debug jobs (spec cost row: ~15 s per state); the toolkit reads up to 1,000 documents
settings.n_pile_eval_source: ours: 64 Pile val rows (512 tokens, 32,704 targets) for the FineWeb-like eval set; the toolkit reads up to 1,000 FineWeb documents of <= 1,024 tokens
settings.control_source: E265's control and its random update, as experiments/adl/results/amend1/predictions.json names them
settings.gap_floor_mult_source: spec 4.2 null path: incr_rel_ce undefined under 3 x the largest |CE_base - CE_ft| of the matched random update, measured in stage 0; a zero gap is always rejected
settings.groups_source: spec 4.3: built pairs (E187's nine, as E264-265 read them), prior-matched (E254/E255) and procedural (E256/E260) states, as E267 read them

stage0.order: first and alone; items refuse unless results/stage0.json says passed
stage0.W0: the do-nothing (an exact zero change) on the control's task: every delta_bar_j norm, every CE_base - CE_ft and every incr_ce (lens, 64 random differences, 64 Gaussians; train, pile and answer sets; all and exclude_pos) exactly 0.0; every incr_rel_ce undefined (zero gap). Any miss stops the job before the control
stage0.control_rule: lowercase_s0, its training windows (E53's hand-write windows, Task.train), subset exclude_pos: the lens's mean over j = 0-4 of incr_ce(delta_bar_j at position j's mask) exceeds the largest of the 64 random differences' same five-position means. A miss: stop; the 67M items do not run
stage0.gap_floor: 3 x the largest |CE_base - CE_ft| of lowercase_s0's random update over its eval sets, subsets and positions; used for every item's incr_rel_ce

control.lens_like_mean: > 0 and above the 64-direction max: medium confidence. Lowercasing shifts every text the same way (a constant vector recovered 0.71 of its gain at the answer position, E143), but its gain was small (1.67 log-odds) and E265's D on the answer reading was read on a different readout
control.A_ours: > its 64-direction null max (our adaptation; reported, not a stop)

control_random.incr_ce: |lens incr_ce| under 0.01 nats at every position (its delta_bar is near 0)

expected.items: descriptive: adl_published_whole_window and answer_target_ce_ours per state with their 64-direction nulls; A_ours (our scalar, the answer-target incr_ce averaged over delta_bar_0..4, nats) beside its null max. No ranking across tasks of the whole-window reading (spec 4.3)

labels.adl_published_whole_window: the toolkit's causal effect (incr_ce, nats) as published, read on the 67M: descriptive
labels.answer_target_ce_ours: our adaptation, not ADL: the same swaps read as the CE of each read row's answer target at its read position
labels.A_ours: our scalar: answer_target_ce_ours lens incr_ce averaged over positions 0-4
